learningObjective: Estimate the throughput impact of warp divergence and identify when divergence does not degrade throughput.

canonicalClaims.claim: Warp divergence penalty applies when threads within a warp take different paths of a branch; the two sides execute serially under lane masking. Warps whose threads take a uniform side incur no divergence cost.
conditions: The branch produces real control divergence (not predicated compile-time),
Threads within a warp truly take different sides.
nonImplications: Does not imply that eliminating all branches always improves performance; small predicated branches are cheap.
Does not imply independent-thread-scheduling makes divergence free; it changes reconvergence semantics without removing serialization.

misconceptions.claim: Divergence is a block-scope property; if any thread in the block diverges, the whole block pays the penalty.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Divergence is a warp-scope property; warps in the same block are independently scheduled.

misconceptions.claim: Volta's independent thread scheduling eliminates warp divergence.
misconceptions.whyWrong: ITS provides per-thread PCs and safer reconvergence, but divergent sides still execute in serial under masking within a warp.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: CUDA C++ Programming Guide, independent thread scheduling notes

misconceptions.claim: Divergent warp time equals max(T_A, T_B), not T_A + T_B.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Lane masking serializes both paths; the warp progresses through both sides in sequence.

implementationFacts: Divergent path cost per warp ≈ sum of side durations for real control flow.
Warp size = 32; a warp's 32 threads share a scheduler.
performanceScenarios: Softmax and reduction kernels align data by warp boundary to avoid divergence in reduction steps.
Sparse-mask kernels often route similar-mask threads into the same warp via pre-sorting to reduce divergence.
